name: Trilobite Echo
identityBoundary: Trilobite Echo is an original Tantalus project lineage derived from the adult Prometheus Trilobite design language. It is not a published caste, not the unique film organism, and must never be described as a 1:1 canon replica.

externalAnchors.use: Official film and continuity anchor for Prometheus (2012); the screen creature remains the primary visual authority.
Official VFX-production confirmation of the concluding Trilobite attack and subsurface-scattering work used for believable translucent skin.
Licensed articulated anatomy and scale cross-check: the creature is presented as a massive tentacled grappler with bendable limbs, spanning almost 17 inches beside a nearly 9-inch Engineer figure.

externalAnchors.authority: Neville Page interview via Blue Screen Reveals
externalAnchors.use: Direct design rationale: the final topology has exactly seven primary tentacles; locomotion uses a powerful raised, knuckle-walk-like support grammar; the underside is a central physiological opening with labial folds.

externalAnchors.authority: Computer Graphics World / Weta VFX supervisor Martin Hill
externalAnchors.use: Production-scale and deformation cross-check: the adult is described as about 14 feet across, with muscular tentacles, longitudinal wrinkles, and skin that becomes lighter and shinier in tension and rougher and darker in compression.
Cross-check of production quotations: seven-tentacle design, powerful lift, cephalopod rather than fossil-trilobite anatomy, and pale milky formaldehyde-squid material reference.

v56Audit.groundingObservation: All sixteen normalized alpha bounds end at y=240, matching the existing 16-pixel lower guard and providing a useful ground-line precedent.
strengths: Dedicated pale wet organic identity with a soft central mantle is already readable.
All sixteen poses face screen right and the four rows already communicate curl/alert, low crawl, grapple/implantation and terminal collapse.
The old runtime establishes a large, low apex envelope distinct from humanoids and adult xenomorphs.
blockingGaps: Primary tentacle paths merge or disappear under overlaps; V56 cannot prove a stable count and attachment topology across all poses.
Some frames read as a pointed fleshy squid with a head-like front rather than one radial mantle and central physiological aperture.
The attack row exposes several fine strands without a strict distinction between the seven load-bearing tentacles and the central implantation apparatus.
The four-frame rows are only broad motion references; V66 requires four dedicated eight-pose chronological boards.
v56Audit.authorityRule: V56 controls project palette, low gameplay scale, lateral readability and broad motion grammar. The reviewed seven-tentacle V66 lock below overrides V56 wherever limb count or attachment is ambiguous.

referenceLock.identity: One large low pale pathogen parasite with no head, eyes, skeleton or humanoid torso: a soft central mantle carrying one ventral implantation apparatus and exactly seven muscular primary tentacles.

topology.attachment: All seven primary tentacles arise independently and continuously from one radial basal ring around the same central mantle hub. Their clockwise order around the ring is immutable across every pose and clip.
topology.continuity: Each primary tentacle must remain traceable from its thick muscular base to one tapered recurved knuckle-like terminal. No primary limb may split, branch, fuse, detach, vanish, swap attachment or be added during attack.
topology.visibility: Controlled overlap is allowed, but every one of the seven continuous base-to-tip paths must remain anatomically accountable; no camera-facing rosette and no unreadable pile of interchangeable strands.
topology.supportFunction: The seven primaries are the only long load-bearing crawl and grapple limbs. Their compressed ends can plant like soft knuckles; they are not rigid xenomorph claws and have no dominant octopus sucker pattern.
topology.centralApparatus: Exactly one ventral central physiological aperture with compact labial folds. During attack it may open and present one short central implantation organ; all such tissue emerges only from this aperture and never becomes an eighth primary tentacle.
topology.secondaryAppendages: No independent secondary locomotive tentacles. Fine folds or short implantation filaments, if suggested, must remain a compact central-aperture detail, be retracted outside the contact phase, and never extend to primary-limb length.

facing.lateralizationKey: The anterior aperture/implantation organ and grapple reach point to screen right while the mantle hub remains central and support tentacles trail or brace behind it.
facing.camera: Strict orthographic gameplay side view. No turnaround, left-facing pose, front-facing radial flower, camera orbit, perspective change or three-quarter portrait.

material.palette: Milky ivory, pale beige-pink and restrained translucent rose-gray with subtle veins and internal tissue.
material.surface: Wet multilayered invertebrate skin with longitudinal folds. Stretched tissue becomes slightly lighter and shinier; compressed tissue becomes darker and rougher in the folds.
material.forbiddenRead: Never black biomechanical carapace, hard fossil shell, realistic blue octopus, rubber toy plastic or adult-xenomorph chitin.

gameplayScale.externalAdultContext: The Prometheus adult is documented at roughly 14 feet tentacle-to-tentacle; this is context, not a literal sprite-world scale mandate.
gameplayScale.projectRole: Large low apex hazard: broader than a marine and visually heavy, but not a room-filling boss or a miniature Facehugger.
gameplayScale.anatomicalScaleInvariant: Compare the central mantle from the posterior radial-attachment centroid to the closed anterior aperture, not total tentacle reach, pose bounding box or curled silhouette. This mantle length and thickness must stay constant across clips.

sourceScaleByClip.rule: Do not authorize per-clip scaling from this reference phase. Future factors require reviewed measurements of the same central-mantle landmarks on every generated source.

sourceContract.background: true transparent RGBA or perfectly uniform opaque #FF00FF
sourceContract.minimumClearanceRule: At least 12 percent of the nominal cell dimension remains empty at every cell boundary; for a 1774 by 887 source this operationally means at least 55 pixels of clean matte around every pose.
sourceContract.cellIsolation: Exactly one complete creature per nominal cell; all seven primary tentacles and the central body stay inside that cell with no touching, crossing, crop, detached fragments or grid lines.

rootAndGround.centralRootDefinition: The physical root is the projection of the central mantle attachment hub onto the support plane, never the lowest or farthest tentacle tip.
rootAndGround.pivotStatus: queue precedent only; requires manual physical-anchor review after generation
rootAndGround.idleAndMove: At least three primary tentacle tips form readable planted supports; the mantle can breathe or translate internally without skating the central root.
rootAndGround.attack: At least two rear primary tentacles remain planted as braces while two forward primaries reach to the right; lifting the mantle must not create an unmotivated airborne root.
rootAndGround.death: Support points fail sequentially. The terminal anchor is beneath the collapsed central mantle, not beneath an extended loose tentacle.

poses: small central lift on planted tentacles
idle.rules: Eight distinct grounded poses; seven primary bases flex subtly, no full-body radial spin and no implantation organ.

move.rules: Low powerful tentacle-driven crawl, fixed central-mantle scale and stable clockwise limb order; no translation inside the cell.

poses: central aperture opens and short implantation organ presents
attack.rules: Exactly seven primary tentacles throughout. No projectile, acid spit, detached filament, added arm or copied film composition.

death.rules: One irreversible loss of support; no recovery, explosion, dissolved body, detached tentacle or nonlethal-hurt reuse.

prohibitions: No eighth primary tentacle and no missing, fused, branched, swapped or newly spawned primary limb.
No head, eyes, skull, elongated dome, dorsal tubes, blade tail, double jaw, humanoid torso, arms or legs.
No hard fossil-trilobite shell, crab-like Facehugger legs, miniature Facehugger, realistic blue octopus or dominant sucker rows.
No projectile spit, acid cannon, weapon, equipment, armor, detached gore stream or free-floating implantation strand.
No black biomechanical adult-xenomorph redesign and no reuse or recolor of another enemy profile.
No left-facing pose, camera-facing radial flower, camera rotation, perspective drift or inconsistent physical scale.
No crop, cell-boundary contact, overlapping cells, scenery, floor, shadow, checkerboard, text, labels, UI, logo or watermark.
No exact recreation of a Prometheus shot and no copied official or licensed bitmap.

referenceResolution.topologyConflict: Computer Graphics World describes six or seven tentacles visible in complex final shots, while creature designer Neville Page explicitly describes the final design decision as seven. The production lock uses exactly seven because it is the direct design intent and provides deterministic animation topology.
referenceResolution.v56Conflict: Any ambiguous V56 overlap or apparent count change is treated as an old asset defect, not a competing anatomy rule.
referenceResolution.scaleResolution: The documented 14-foot film adult is retained as biological context; the project-owned 184 by 104 runtime envelope controls gameplay readability.
